facts.headline: The world's oldest operating Ferris wheel survived being burned to a skeleton
facts.body_html: The Riesenrad opened in Prater park in 1897 and is the oldest Ferris wheel still running anywhere on Earth. It was gutted by fire in 1944 and rebuilt with half its original 30 cabins — then went on to star in The Third Man.

facts.headline: 230,000 roof tiles form a Habsburg eagle you can only see from above
facts.body_html: St. Stephen's Cathedral's zigzag roof is covered in 230,000 glazed tiles in ten colors, arranged into a double-headed eagle on one side and Vienna's coat of arms on the other — all visible only from a height.

facts.headline: A 6-year-old Mozart reportedly proposed marriage after slipping on this floor
facts.body_html: In 1762, six-year-old Wolfgang Mozart performed for the imperial family in Schönbrunn's Hall of Mirrors, slipped on the polished floor, and was helped up by young Archduchess Marie Antoinette — he's said to have promised to marry her on the spot.
suggested_queries: Schonbrunn Palace Hall of Mirrors interior

facts.headline: This is the only place left where 16th-century horsemanship is still performed exactly as written
facts.body_html: The Spanish Riding School's white Lipizzaner stallions have trained in the Hofburg's baroque Winter Riding School since 1735 — the last place on Earth still practicing classical haute école dressage in its original, unbroken form.

facts.headline: An empress once had gym equipment installed inside this palace to control her waist
facts.body_html: Empress Elisabeth ("Sisi") kept her waist near 19 inches her entire adult life, wrapping herself in damp cloths and installing personal workout equipment in her Hofburg apartments — extreme even by Habsburg standards.

facts.headline: Mozart has a grave here — he just isn't in it
facts.body_html: Vienna's Central Cemetery holds a place of honor for Mozart among Beethoven, Schubert, and Strauss — but it's a memorial, not a burial. His actual grave, in a different Vienna cemetery, was unmarked and its exact spot was lost.

facts.headline: Vienna is the only capital city on Earth that still grows its own wine
facts.body_html: Over 600 hectares of working vineyards sit inside Vienna's city limits, legally protected from ever becoming anything but vineyard. The blend grown there, Wiener Gemischter Satz, can't legally be made anywhere else.
